data.name: My Ex-Boyfriend the Space Tyrant
data.detailed_description:
What would this gay space hero be like? The answer is he's a charmer -

Smarter than it needs to be ... a light-hearted adventure -

Introduction

My Ex-Boyfriend the Space Tyrant is a traditional point-and-click adventure but stands out for its gay cast and eye-catching visuals.

On the surface, the storyline is standard science fiction fare: you play as retired space captain Tycho Minogue, dragged back into active service in order to foil the nefarious plans of a powerful interplanetary tyrant who is taking his fleet from world to world, subjugating the free people of the galaxy. But there are twists! A tale of love, loss and adventure spread over three planets and several lightyears, My Ex-Boyfriend the Space Tyrant is a classic of the gay game genre.

Some Key Features

  • Full length gay themed point-and-click adventure game
  • A superb blend of comedy, drama, romance and mystery
  • Artwork by award winning artist Joe Phillips
  • Over 70 scenes and 40 characters
  • Source included
  • Accessibility options for vision and hearing impaired players

What The Fans Are Saying

Thank you for a wonderful game playing experience, and the fact that it was a 'gay game' made it ever so much more enjoyable for this gay player. - John

I'd like to compliment you on the game, My Ex-boyfriend the Space Tyrant. I enjoyed the artwork, the tongue-in-cheekiness, and the sense of a campy space-adventure. It's nice to have a gay-centric game, especially since most games are heavily influenced to appeal to the straight guy-gamer. - Jason

It's a whole lot of fun, as a gay guy this is the game I've wanted to play all my life! - Brian

reviews.review:
My Ex-Boyfriend the Space Tyrant is a deliberately unconventional point-and-click adventure that takes the familiar structure of a science-fiction rescue story and gives it a much more personal, romantic, and campy identity. Developed and published by Up Multimedia, it centers on retired space captain Tycho Minogue, who is drawn back into interplanetary trouble when a powerful tyrant begins imposing his rule across the galaxy. What initially resembles a straightforward battle between hero and villain soon develops into something more personal, combining Tycho's history and relationships with the larger conflict. The result is an adventure built around comedy, romance, mystery, loss, and science-fiction absurdity rather than action or spectacle.

Gameplay follows the traditions of classic point-and-click adventures. Exploration, conversations, environmental observation, item collection, and puzzle solving form the core of the experience. Instead of testing reflexes, the game encourages players to investigate each location carefully and determine how characters, objects, and clues fit together. Its mechanics are intentionally old-fashioned, which works well for players who enjoy traditional adventure games but may feel somewhat rigid to anyone accustomed to more streamlined modern narrative titles. The slower pace also means that much of the enjoyment depends on appreciating the writing and personalities rather than expecting constant mechanical variety.

The story benefits greatly from its unusual protagonist and openly gay perspective. Tycho is not simply a generic space captain with a different romantic preference added as a minor character detail. His identity and relationship history are integrated into the adventure itself, allowing romance to become part of the larger science-fiction narrative. This gives the game a personality that separates it from many conventional space adventures. The writing frequently approaches its universe with tongue-in-cheek humor, but it also makes room for more sincere ideas involving relationships, separation, affection, and personal history. The combination of comedy and emotional material prevents the story from becoming nothing more than a prolonged parody.

Its visual presentation is another defining characteristic. Artwork by Joe Phillips gives the characters an expressive illustrated appearance that suits the flamboyant tone. The game favors colorful comic-style imagery over realistic environments, creating a visual identity that complements its eccentric cast and exaggerated interplanetary setting. With more than 70 scenes and approximately 40 characters described on its Steam page, there is a respectable amount of environmental and character variety. Traveling across three planets helps the adventure maintain a sense of progression, even though the actual interaction remains grounded in traditional point-and-click mechanics.

The supporting cast contributes considerably to the experience because conversations are just as important as puzzles. Meeting new personalities provides opportunities for humor, clues, character development, and occasional romantic or dramatic moments. The mystery component gives these interactions additional purpose, as players are not merely moving between locations but gradually uncovering the circumstances surrounding the larger conflict. This blend of personal storytelling and galactic adventure gives the narrative more substance than its intentionally silly premise might initially suggest.

Puzzle design remains closely connected to the genre's classic conventions. Players should expect to examine environments, collect objects, speak with characters, and experiment with possible solutions. This can produce satisfying moments when clues finally connect, although it also brings some of the frustrations traditionally associated with older point-and-click design. Progress can occasionally depend on recognizing the intended logic rather than an immediately obvious solution. Anyone who enjoys methodically searching scenes and trying different approaches should be comfortable with this structure, while players who prefer continuously guided progression may find certain stretches slower.

Accessibility deserves recognition as well. The game specifically includes options intended to assist players with vision and hearing impairments, an especially useful consideration for an adventure that depends heavily on visual information and written dialogue. Its single-player format also allows the experience to be approached at an individual pace without competitive pressure. The inclusion of these accessibility considerations strengthens what is otherwise a fairly traditional adventure-game package.

Steam Deck compatibility is less definitive. Steam does not currently present the title with a clear official Steam Deck compatibility classification on its store page. However, the game has Linux support and full controller support listed in Steam metadata, both of which are encouraging characteristics for handheld use. Because there is no confirmed Valve Deck rating, it is better regarded as potentially playable rather than guaranteed to provide a completely trouble-free experience. Players interested specifically in Steam Deck play should therefore be prepared for the possibility of compatibility adjustments or interface quirks rather than assuming Verified-level functionality.

The game's greatest limitation is also inseparable from its charm. It is unapologetically niche. Players looking for elaborate combat, cinematic production values, complex role-playing systems, or fast-paced science-fiction action will not find those things here. Instead, the emphasis remains firmly on illustrated environments, dialogue, puzzle solving, humor, romance, and character interaction. Its presentation can feel modest compared with larger adventure productions, while its traditional mechanics occasionally reveal their age. Yet the same qualities allow the writing and distinctive artistic personality to remain at the center of the experience.

Ultimately, this is a memorable adventure because it knows exactly what kind of story it wants to tell. Rather than attempting to revolutionize point-and-click gameplay, it uses an established format to deliver an eccentric gay-centered science-fiction story filled with colorful characters, romantic complications, mystery, comedy, and emotional undertones. Its mechanical conservatism and niche humor will prevent it from appealing equally to everyone, but players receptive to classic adventure design and unusual storytelling should find considerable charm in its journey across the galaxy.

Rating: 7/10
